solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 22 down to 24); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dish seen in fine old dresser

definitions.meaning: an 18th-century dandy who affected Continental fashions was called a ...

explanation.surface: A meal spotted inside an elegant antique sideboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' suggests furniture, but here it is a person who dresses: the Georgian fop of 'Yankee Doodle' fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta served as a meal is a dish, and the Georgian fop was a well-known type of showy dresser.

clue.text: Hymn from the works by European variously recalled at intervals

parts.note: the works means everything, all

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the picked letters run backwards
at intervals takes every other letter of variously

explanation.surface: A hymn drawn from a European composer's works, recalled at odd moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' picks AIUL from vArIoUsLy; 'recalled' turns that to LUIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleluia is a song of praise to God, sung as or in a hymn.

clue.text: A page of baseless, false old stories

indicators.note: false means wrong, so the letters are rearranged into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A page of groundless, untrue tales from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baseless' reads as a description of the stories, but the whole word is anagram fodder; 'false' is the signal, leaving 'old stories' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop's Fables are ancient Greek moral tales about animals, very old stories indeed.

clue.text: Duo I left floundering in the deep

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pair of swimmers left struggling in deep water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the deep' suggests the sea; in cricket the deep is the outfield, far from the batsman. 'floundering' rearranges DUOILEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, fielders in the deep stand near the boundary, which is the outfield.

clue.text: Reserve power needed for small cooler

parts.note: ice means cold reserve of manner
a cube is a number raised to the third power

explanation.surface: Emergency electricity required for a little fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power' suggests electricity; it is the mathematical power, here the third.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cube is a little block of frozen water dropped into a drink to chill it.

clue.text: Face family, cold, having received welcome earlier

indicators.note: earlier means the received greeting comes before the cold letter

parts.note: got means received
hi is a word of welcome
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Meeting relatives in the cold after an earlier warm greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' means typeface, not a human face.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is a group of related typefaces (blackletter or sans-serif), a type family in printing.

clue.text: Useless little film receiving Oscar

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: vid is a short form of video
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A worthless short movie wins an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award; it is the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something void, like a void contract, has no legal force and is therefore of no use.

clue.text: Run, when in better shape, at first without a stitch

indicators.note: when in means the letter sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a staker is someone who bets, a better
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of shape

explanation.surface: Going jogging once fitter, but initially in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like an adjective about fitness; it is one who bets. STARKERS is British slang for naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a stitch on means wearing nothing at all, which is what the slang word means.

clue.text: Boast pay can secure plant

parts.note: to crow is to boast
to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Bragging that wages can buy a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can secure' is a link phrase: the two pieces together can give the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowfoot is a buttercup-family flowering plant with leaves shaped like a bird's foot.

clue.text: Luxury's endless advantage

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the synonym for luxury is dropped

parts.note: plush means luxurious; here as a noun sense of luxury

explanation.surface: A life of luxury has a never-ending upside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the H from PLUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a benefit or point in favour, a synonym of advantage.

clue.text: Incumbent at first on females, one not so friendly, to relay pardon

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word on is taken

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female; two of them give FF
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: read as re-lay: the word for pardon is laid into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: colder means less friendly
Eh? is said when asking someone to repeat themselves, like Pardon?

explanation.surface: A sitting official, relying on women and a frosty figure, passes on a pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to relay' is read as re-lay, an unusual containment signal: the word for pardon is laid within the word for less friendly, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An incumbent is the current holder of a post, i.e. someone holding an office.

clue.text: Go, feeling one's leaving for long time

parts.note: go means energy or vitality, as does life

indicators.note: leaving means going out, so the numeral is taken away

parts.note: sentience is the capacity for feeling
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Depart, sensing that someone is quitting for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops the I from SENTIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence is imprisonment for life, a long time in jail, crossword shorthand for a long stretch.

clue.text: Follow United, again in the money for winning

indicators.note: the second U goes inside, 'again' because the prize word already holds one U

parts.note: a purse is prize money for a race or fight
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: Supporters following Manchester United back in the prize money again.
explanation.walkthrough: PURSE already contains a U, so adding another is doing it 'again'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue someone is to chase or follow them.

clue.text: Report of engine trouble — sponsor getting sack

parts.note: to back someone is to sponsor or support them
to fire is to sack from a job

explanation.surface: A motoring report: the team's financial backer is dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A backfire is the loud bang from an engine when fuel ignites in the exhaust, a noisy sign of trouble.

clue.text: A villain tailed by Sherlock, ultimately for sport

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the detective's name
having its tail cut off, so the synonym for villain loses its last letter

parts.note: a baddie is a villain

explanation.surface: A criminal is followed by Sherlock Holmes, in the end for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailed' reads as shadowed by a detective, but it means docked: BADDIE loses its E. 'by' sets the K beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabaddi is a South Asian team contact game, so it is an example of a sport.

clue.text: Family's experiences after descending on a foreign city

indicators.note: after here means following, so the experiencing word comes after the family word
in a down clue the family's experiences come down onto the letter a, sitting above it

parts.note: kin is family; with the apostrophe s it gives kin's
to have something is to experience it, so he has means he experiences

explanation.surface: Relatives' adventures after landing on a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'descending on' puts KINSHAS above A.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinshasa is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, a city abroad for a Times reader.

clue.text: Old shipping magnate's donkey rides?

parts.note: the tycoon's surname split up reads as a phrase about someone being on a donkey

explanation.surface: Holiday treats on the beach laid on by a Greek tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the surname as ON ASS IS: a rider 'is on ass', which is what donkey rides are. Aristotle Onassis was the Greek shipping tycoon who married Jacqueline Kennedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle Onassis was the twentieth-century Greek shipowner, and his name broken up describes riding a donkey.

clue.text: Romantic piece: hit performance listened out for

indicators.note: listened out for means heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a knock is a hit and a turn is a performance, so knock turn

explanation.surface: A romantic number, a hit, eagerly awaited by its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit performance' suggests a smash show; it is KNOCK + TURN, which when spoken matches the music.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a dreamy piano piece of the Romantic era, as written by Chopin.

clue.text: Thing that's crossed channel that is crossing river? Correct

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across, so the abbreviation goes round the rest

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
to fix something is to correct it

explanation.surface: A ship that crossed a channel goes over a river, true enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' is the English Channel: a French expression that came over into English. 'Thing' is slang for an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: An idée fixe is an obsession, a 'thing' about something, and the phrase is borrowed from French.

clue.text: Main unit for broadcasters opening in Yale?

parts.note: key means main, as in a key point

indicators.note: broadcasters speak on air, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a whole is a complete unit

explanation.surface: The chief measure for a radio station at a famous American university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yale' suggests the university; it is the lock brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yale is a brand of door lock, and the keyhole is the slot in a lock that takes the key.

clue.text: Peers into vessel, bonnet having been pulled back

indicators.note: the run of letters is read backwards, as if drawn back
the letters are found inside the following two words

explanation.surface: Someone looks into a ship after their hat has been pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' looks like a verb meaning looks, but it is the noun: ESSELBON, from vESSEL BONnet, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The noblesse is the nobility as a class, collectively the peers of the realm.

clue.text: Daily rounds too much, having to go to North London suburb

indicators.note: rounds means goes around, so the paper encloses the other piece

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means too much

explanation.surface: A newspaper's rounds are excessive, having to cover north London too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' looks part of the definition, but Sutton is in south London: 'having to go to North' turns OTT upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutton is a borough on the southern edge of Greater London, a suburb of the capital.

clue.text: Trick with needle to get swelling out

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
to needle someone is to vex or irritate them

explanation.surface: A sleight of hand with a sewing needle to deal with a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A convex surface curves outward, bulging rather than hollowed.

clue.text: Laughter about need to employ such a search?

indicators.note: about means around, so the laughter goes round the next piece

parts.note: ho ho represents laughter
to have use to is an old sense of needing to
to use something is to employ it

explanation.surface: Mocking a police search that needs to employ every officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. The definition leans on the rest of the clue (semi-&lit): a search conducted door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: A house-to-house search is police inquiry calling at every home in an area in turn.

clue.text: There's a problem for all to see: ball trapped between rugby posts?

parts.note: U is the British film rating for universal viewing, suitable for all

indicators.note: trapped between means the ball sits inside the posts

parts.note: rugby goalposts are H-shaped, so two posts give two Hs
O is ball-shaped

explanation.surface: A problem in plain view: the ball stuck between the goalposts.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-oh is the exclamation someone makes on noticing trouble, spoken in place of the phrase.

clue.text: Something one might file away secure?

definitions.meaning: a fingernail is filed down with a ... file

explanation.surface: An office item to be archived and kept safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'file away' suggests putting papers in a cabinet; here it is filing down a fingernail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingernail is shaped with an emery file, and to fasten with a pin hammered in is to fix firmly.

clue.text: Bird finally chooses this moment to cry out

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of chooses

parts.note: now means at this moment
to yowl is to cry out loudly

explanation.surface: A bird at last picks its moment to call.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowy owl is a large white Arctic owl, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Name of E number originally used in topping

indicators.note: used in means placed inside the slang word

parts.note: beezer is old British schoolboy slang for excellent, as is topping

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of number

explanation.surface: A food label naming the E number found in a dessert topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' looks like a cake decoration, but it is dated British slang for first-rate, like BEEZER (Beano-comic speak).
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer is a man's first name, as in Ebenezer Scrooge, so an example of a name.
